title: Freespace “twistronics”: moiré structured light for optical supertopologies
abstract: Twistronics, the study of moir\'e superlattices of twisted bilayer 2D materials creating nontrivial physical effects, has recently revolutionized diverse subjects from materials to optoelectronics, nanophotonics, and beyond. Here, breaking the reliance on materials, we present twistronics in higher-dimensional free space, where the twisted lattice is not a layer of 2D material but a 3D propagating light field with topological textures. Moir\'e structured light with a twist angle can generate a rich set of high-dimensional topologies, including skyrmionium bags, skyrmion bag superlattices, skyrmion clusters, and optical quasicrystals, with controllable symmetry. Many of these textures have not been reported before. Importantly, in contrast to prior moir\'e superlattices, our freespace optical moir\'e textures maintain their topologies over a long propagation distances, showing nondiffractive behavior and robustness against perturbations and obstacles. Our work unlocks higher dimensions to manipulate moir\'e photonics with high-capacity topologies to address modern challenges of robust information transfer and encryption.

title: ДАВЛАТ ОРГАНЛАРИ ВА ТАШКИЛОТЛАРИ ФАОЛИЯТИДА КОРРУПЦИЯВИЙ ХАВФ-ХАТАРЛАРНИ АНИҚЛАШ ВА БАҲОЛАШНИНГ НАЗАРИЙ-ҲУҚУҚИЙ ЖИҲАТЛАРИ
journal: Central Asian Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Management Studies
abstract: Ушбу мақолада давлат органлари ва ташкилотлари фаолиятида коррупциявий хавф-хатарларни аниқлаш, баҳолаш ва уларни бошқариш (риск-менежмент) тизимининг мазмун-моҳияти, назарий-ҳуқуқий асослари ҳамда амалий аҳамияти таҳлил қилинган. Тадқиқотда ватандош ва хорижий олимларнинг (А.В.Кудашкин, В.В.Астанин, Ж.Шкрбец, А.Макдевитт, Ж.Жонстон ва бошқ.) илмий қарашлари ҳамда халқаро стандартлар (ISO 37001, FATF) қиёсий ўрганилган. Шунингдек, давлат ташкилотларида жараёнларга йўналтирилган ёндашув асосида хавф-хатарлар харитаси ва комплаенс-назорат механизмларини такомиллаштириш бўйича муаллифлик таклиф ва тавсиялари илгари сурилган.

title: Who benefits from new work? Employee perceptions and justice evaluations in family businesses
abstract: Purpose The transformation toward new work creates opportunities and challenges, as workplace flexibility benefits blue- and white-collar employees unevenly. This study examines how blue- and white-collar employees experience and perceive new work practices in family businesses, focusing on organizational justice. By comparing family businesses and a non-family business, the study investigates how occupational roles and organizational contexts shape employee responses to new work measures. Design/methodology/approach The study adopts a qualitative multiple-case study design based on 27 semi-structured interviews across three German family firms and one non-family firm in traditional industries. Data were analyzed using qualitative content analysis. Findings The findings reveal a paradox: although blue-collar workers face limited access to flexibility measures, they do not perceive distributive injustice, attributing limitations to occupational constraints. However, interpersonal justice concerns arise through reduced accessibility of decision-makers in hybrid work. While organizations differ in their implementation approaches, justice mechanisms remain consistent across contexts. Originality/value This study offers one of the first qualitative comparisons of blue- and white-collar employees' new work experiences in family and non-family firms. It challenges a core assumption of organizational justice theory by showing that fairness judgments hinge on occupational legitimacy rather than outcome equality and surfaces an overlooked interpersonal justice cost of hybrid work. For family business theory, it clarifies the boundary conditions of family ownership: family-specific values shape the form of new work implementation, whereas occupational constraints more strongly shape employee justice perceptions.

title: When evaluating ideas exposes the evaluator: leader impostor thoughts and the obstruction of employee creativity
abstract: Purpose Leaders’ evaluation and development of employee ideas shape employee creativity. Yet how leaders respond to employee ideas when they perceive others to evaluate their professional competence more favorably than they evaluate it themselves, and how these responses are subsequently associated with employee creativity, remain largely underexplored. Grounded in self-presentation theory, this study examines how leader impostor thoughts are associated with different responses to employee ideas, identifies employee creative reputation as a boundary condition, and provides theoretical support and practical guidance for organizational idea management practices. Design/methodology/approach The hypothesized model was tested across two complementary studies: a three-wave multisource field study with 176 matched supervisor-employee dyads, and a 2 × 2 between-subjects scenario experiment involving 248 managers. Findings Consistent results were observed across both studies. Leader impostor thoughts were positively associated with leader idea rejection when employee creative reputation was low, but negatively associated with creative-idea developmental feedback when employee creative reputation was high. The field study further showed that both conditional pathways are linked to lower employee creativity, forming two distinct obstructive patterns: selection-based obstruction and development-based obstruction. Originality/value From a self-presentational perspective, this study develops a bidirectional account of leader idea gatekeeping by bringing the evaluator’s own professional image into explanations of gatekeeping and explaining why leader impostor thoughts may be associated with differentiated rather than uniform responses to employee ideas. It also extends the creative reputation literature by identifying creative reputation as a social-evaluative cue that structures the meaning of leaders’ gatekeeping responses. Furthermore, by distinguishing the selection function of idea rejection from the developmental function of creative-idea developmental feedback, it offers implications for organizational idea management and leadership development.

title: Toxic leadership behaviour as a predictor of turnover intention among nurses in a Bangladeshi healthcare context: A conservation of resources perspective
journal: SA Journal of Human Resource Management
abstract: Orientation: Toxic leadership behaviour has become a critical organisational challenge in healthcare and is associated with poorer employee well-being and higher turnover intention. Research purpose: This study examined the relationship between toxic leadership behaviour and turnover intention and assessed whether organisational culture mediates this relationship among nurses in a large tertiary public hospital in Bangladesh. Motivation for the study: Although toxic leadership has attracted growing scholarly attention, empirical evidence on its relationship with organisational culture and turnover intention in developing-country healthcare contexts remains limited. Research approach/design and method: This study employed a quantitative, cross-sectional research design. Data were collected from 203 registered nurses, and partial least squares structural equation modelling was used to test hypotheses. Main findings: Toxic leadership behaviour significantly and positively predicted turnover intention. It also significantly and negatively predicted organisational culture. However, organisational culture did not significantly predict turnover intention, and the mediating effect of organisational culture was not supported. Practical/managerial implications: Healthcare organisations should prioritise leadership assessment, monitoring and development initiatives to address toxic leadership and support workforce retention. Contribution/value-add: This study extends the application of conservation of resources theory by demonstrating that toxic leadership behaviour is positively associated with turnover intention and negatively associated with organisational culture in a demanding healthcare environment. It further contributes by providing evidence that organisational culture did not mediate the relationship between toxic leadership behaviour and turnover intention among nurses in a Bangladeshi healthcare context.

title: Spatial pattern evolution and its driving factors for the fruit industry in China
abstract: In this study, we investigate China’s fruit production patterns, spatial evolution characteristics, and driving factors, with the goal of providing scientific evidence surrounding the high-quality development of the fruit industry. Based on the provincial panel data of fruit production in China from 2000 to 2024, this study explores the spatial evolution characteristics of China’s fruit industry using the production concentration index, the production scale index, the gravity center migration model, and the standard deviational ellipse model; further, we explore the factors influencing the fruit industry using the spatial autocorrelation analysis and the spatial Durbin model. The results show that the gravity center of fruit production in China has been consistently shifting westward, with this trend showing signs of further intensification. Notably, significant spatial autocorrelation and spatial spillover effects exist in China’s fruit production distribution, with spatial dependence particularly strengthening progressively in western regions. The spatial variation in fruit production in China is influenced by certain factors: sunshine hours, disaster intensity, comparative returns, urbanization level, effective irrigation area, technological progress, and fiscal agricultural policies. Meanwhile, the degree of impact exerted by these driving factors on changes in production distribution varies significantly across different fruit-producing regions. Therefore, based on the spatial dynamics of China’s fruit production patterns, in this article, we propose that the spatial distribution of fruit production is optimized by leveraging region-specific resource endowments. Simultaneously, it is important to fully harness technological progress, as the primary driver, and to effectively capitalize on the positive spillover effects from other contributing factors. Accordingly, it is possible to enhance the industry’s support systems, with the ultimate goal of achieving the optimized spatial distribution of fruit production in China.

title: Re-examining the intent to stay scale: Evidence from Generation Z employees in Indonesia
abstract: Orientation: Employee retention remains an important concern in organisational and industrial psychology as Generation Z becomes increasingly visible in the workforce. In Indonesia, the applicability of established retention measures requires empirical examination. Research purpose: This study examines the psychometric properties of the Indonesian version of the Intent to Stay Scale (ITS) among Generation Z employees in Indonesia, specifically internal consistency reliability and convergent validity. Motivation for the study: Although intent to stay is widely used as an indicator of employee retention, evidence regarding measurement properties across contexts remains limited. This is particularly relevant for Generation Z employees in Indonesia. Research approach/design and method: A structured contextual harmonisation and pre-testing process was followed by field testing and psychometric evaluation. Data were collected through an online survey from 461 Generation Z employees in Indonesia who met the criteria and passed response-quality screening. Item-level analyses were conducted using jamovi, while the reflective measurement model was evaluated using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 3. Main findings: All six ITS items demonstrated acceptable outer loadings, ranging from 0.739 to 0.897. The scale demonstrated satisfactory internal consistency reliability, with Cronbach’s alpha of 0.915, rho_A of 0.923, and composite reliability of 0.934. The average variance extracted was 0.704, providing evidence of convergent validity. Intent to Stay Scale 6 showed the lowest loading but remained above the threshold and was retained. Practical/managerial implications: The findings suggest that the Indonesian ITS may provide useful information when assessing intention to stay among Generation Z employees. Contribution/value-add: This study provides preliminary, context-specific evidence regarding the measurement properties of the Indonesian ITS among Generation Z employees in Indonesia and highlights the importance of evaluating retention measures within contexts.

title: Population genetic analysis of 23 autosomal STR loci in northwestern Türkiye (Bursa)
When the algorithm feels like mine: personalisation depth, algorithmic transparency and psychological ownership in continued streaming engagement
journal: Journal of Research in Interactive Marketing
abstract: Purpose This study examines whether artificial intelligence (AI) personalisation depth and algorithmic transparency relate to continued engagement with streaming platforms through consumers’ psychological ownership of the recommendation stream, and over what range of privacy concern the transparency route holds. Design/methodology/approach A 14-day, two-wave panel of streaming subscribers in Türkiye (N = 450) was analysed with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) and re-estimated with covariance-based SEM. A 2 × 2 between-subjects experiment (N = 236) manipulated both features. Findings Personalisation depth showed an indirect-only mediation pattern through ownership in the estimated model, with a direct path practically equivalent to zero within a pre-specified bound; the pattern replicated under random assignment. Ownership carried 45 per cent of the association between transparency and engagement, and a direct path accounted for the rest. The transparency–ownership link was no longer significant above a privacy-concern level of about 4.5 (7-point scale), a region holding roughly two in five respondents. Platform involvement strengthened the personalisation route; no group difference was detected for transparency. Research limitations/implications Participants were subscribers aged 18–35 in three Turkish cities, engagement was self-reported and ownership and engagement were measured on the same occasion. Practical implications Ownership measures can complement viewing and churn metrics when personalisation is evaluated, and layered explanations let users choose how much detail they see. Originality/value For interactive marketing, the study recasts the AI feed as a possession consumers co-produce, not exposure firms deliver. It tests, and does not assume, whether design features keep a direct relationship with engagement once ownership is modelled.
